method: Inspected all six context_grid.jpg and all six input_grid.jpg as time-ordered images; additionally inspected025 legacy_contact_detail.jpg. Native-order continuous clips were prepared but no independent human motion review was collected.
scope: Early-input phase plausibility only; not exact contact/validity/terminal-event judgement or tracking accuracy.

findings.input_observation: F2259..F2319 shows server recovery and opponent response, followed by the near-left player's low ready/stroke preparation. This is consistent with the same ongoing service-led play.

findings.service_sequence_observation: Near-right overhead service and forward recovery lead into far-side return preparation. Near-left teammate remains involved in play.
findings.input_observation: F4253..F4313 covers far-side response and the near-left player's preparation to receive the next ball. Subsequent exchange movements continue beyond the fixed input end.

findings.service_sequence_observation: Near-right overhead service is followed by the far receiver's movement and near player's recovery, without a visible intervening reset.
findings.input_observation: F8648..F8708 shows a continuous receiving/recovery sequence. The near-right player subsequently runs and prepares a further groundstroke.

findings.service_sequence_observation: Near-right overhead service is followed by far-side reception and both near players' ready positions.
findings.input_observation: F15593..F15653 shows the service-led receiving sequence. Later frames show another ball response and stroke preparation instead of a return to service preparation.

findings.service_sequence_observation: Near-right player swings from a low racket position upward around the legacy nominal contact. Detail framesF59960..F60012 are consistent with an underhand-type service action rather than an overhead-service template; style and exact contact are not independently labelled.
findings.input_observation: F60006..F60066 follows the service swing with far-side receiving response and near player's readiness. Later the near player runs left for the continuing exchange. No interval shift is made to avoid the four missing initial requested times.
findings.special_limitation: Legacy contact precision remains unknown; a nominal singleton is not a zero-width validated error interval. Overhead-only automatic start detection may miss this type of service.

findings.service_sequence_observation: The distant-side service-led action is followed by near-right reception. Distant ball/contact detail is small; the inherited revised contact bracket is not newly narrowed.
findings.input_observation: F125911..F125971 shows near-right receiver movement, racket swing and follow-through; the far side then responds, with continued near-side ball response later. No point-end/reset indication is visible within the inspected input sequence.
